RESULT read := the target is `putnam_2025_a4`, an `IsLeast` statement with answer `3`, and the single `sorry` is the whole proof.

GOAL prove := `3 ∈ S` and `∀ k ∈ S, 3 ≤ k`, where S is the set of k admitting 2025 k-by-k real matrices with the stated commutation pattern.

FACT lower_bound_sketch := for k = 0, 1 all matrices commute, so S contains no k ≤ 1. For k = 2, A_1 commutes with A_0 and A_2, A_1 is non-scalar (else it commutes with A_3), so A_0 and A_2 lie in span(I, A_1), which is commutative, contradicting that A_0, A_2 do not commute.

HYP membership := a concrete family of 2025 real 3×3 matrices with commuting graph exactly the cycle C_2025 (plus loops) exists.

PLAN membership_check := find an explicit construction for the membership half.

INFER no_strict_upper_construction <- FACT: for strictly upper-triangular 3×3 families A = N + xE + yF, commutation is det(q_i, q_j) = 0 with q = p − c, which is an equivalence relation (parallelism). A cycle graph is not an equivalence relation, so this family cannot work.

INFER needs_nonlinear_family <- INFER no_strict_upper_construction: any construction must use parameters that depend nonlinearly on the index, for example points on a circle at angles 2πk/2025 with commutation encoded by a polynomial in cos(2π(i−j)/2025) that vanishes exactly at differences 0 and ±1.

CHECK feasibility := such a family would need explicit commutator polynomials for 3×3 matrices, plus a Lean proof that cos(2πk/2025) equals 1 or cos(2π/2025) only for k ≡ 0, ±1 (mod 2025), applied across all 2025² index pairs without `decide` or `native_decide`.

RESULT feasibility := I did not find a 3×3 family with this exact commuting graph, and the formalization would be a large project beyond this task. The lower bound is sketched above but not written into Lean, since the membership half is open.

I give up.

I did not modify `/work/putnam_2025_a4.lean`, and it still contains the `sorry`.
